items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: I want ___ a train ticket.
items.explanation: Want takes to + basic verb: want to buy.

rationales.buy: After want, use to before the action verb.
rationales.to buy: Want takes to + basic verb: want to buy.
rationales.to buying: Use buy, not buying, after this to.
rationales.bought: Bought is a past form; want needs to buy here.

findings: Study item had generic feedback and a repeatedly used want frame.
audit.microSkill: Want followed by to-infinitive
audit.pedagogicalValue: Connects a wish to the action wanted.
audit.levelReason: A short ticket-purchase sentence suits A1.
audit.similarityNote: The only direct want-plus-action form task.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: My father is learning ___ a computer.
items.explanation: Learn to + verb describes learning how to do something.

rationales.to use: Learn to + verb describes learning how to do something.
rationales.use: Learn needs to before use in this sentence.
rationales.to used: Use the basic form use after to, not used.
rationales.uses: Uses cannot follow learning here; say learning to use.

findings: Names-on-form necessity reused need and supplied no diagnostic messages.
audit.microSkill: Learn to for acquiring a skill
audit.pedagogicalValue: Introduces the infinitive after learning.
audit.levelReason: Computer use is familiar adult A1 content.
audit.similarityNote: An acquired skill differs from wanting or hoping for an action.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: Do you enjoy ___ for friends?
items.explanation: Enjoy + -ing describes an activity you find pleasant.

rationales.to cook: Enjoy takes cooking, not to cook.
rationales.cook: Use the -ing form of the action after enjoy.
rationales.cooking: Enjoy + -ing describes an activity you find pleasant.
rationales.cooked: Cooked is a past form; it does not name the activity after enjoy.

findings: Music item mixed the listening pattern with a missing preposition and generic explanations.
audit.microSkill: Enjoy followed by an -ing activity
audit.pedagogicalValue: Uses an activity form inside a social question.
audit.levelReason: A short question about cooking fits A1 interaction.
audit.similarityNote: Question form and social enjoyment distinguish it from other verb complements.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: We hope ___ an apartment near work.
items.explanation: Hope to + verb expresses a desired future action.

rationales.renting: Hope does not take renting directly in this sentence; use hope to rent.
rationales.rent: Put to before rent after hope.
rationales.to rented: To is followed by the basic verb rent, not rented.
rationales.to rent: Hope to + verb expresses a desired future action.

findings: Lesson-start item shared boilerplate and a repeatedly used hope pattern.
audit.microSkill: Hope to for a desired future
audit.pedagogicalValue: Connects hope with a future housing action.
audit.levelReason: Simple housing and work vocabulary suit A1.
audit.similarityNote: Future hope differs from a present wish to buy a ticket.

items.setupText: Choose the activity word that completes the sentence correctly.
items.taskText: ___ is my favorite way to travel around town.
items.explanation: Cycling names an activity and can be the subject before is.

rationales.Cycle: The basic verb alone cannot be the subject of this statement.
rationales.Cycling: Cycling names an activity and can be the subject before is.
rationales.Cycles: Cycles is plural, so it cannot fit this singular activity statement with is.
rationales.Cycled: Cycled describes a past action; it does not name the activity here.

findings: Children-playing sentence duplicated want-to selection and lacked adult context.
audit.microSkill: An -ing activity as subject
audit.pedagogicalValue: Shows that an activity can be what a sentence is about.
audit.levelReason: One familiar travel activity supports a basic A1 subject phrase.
audit.similarityNote: Sentence begins with an activity instead of a person's name.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence to say why you went to the market.
items.taskText: I went to the market ___ some fruit.
items.explanation: To buy gives the reason for going: buying fruit was your purpose.

rationales.bought: A past verb cannot connect this purpose to went without another clause.
rationales.buy: The basic verb needs to when it gives the purpose of going.
rationales.to buy: To buy gives the reason for going: buying fruit was your purpose.
rationales.to buying: A purpose phrase uses to + basic verb, not to buying.

findings: Sandwich planning item reused a subject-verb-blank frame and boilerplate.
audit.microSkill: Infinitive of purpose
audit.pedagogicalValue: Explains why an everyday journey was made.
audit.levelReason: Market and fruit give concrete A1 support for a purpose phrase.
audit.similarityNote: The infinitive explains a reason rather than completing want or hope.

items.setupText: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
items.taskText: Describe an activity that gives you pleasure.
options: I like to reading travel books.
items.explanation: Like can take an -ing activity. Like to read would also be grammatical, but it is not one of these options.

After like, use reading or to read, not read alone.
To takes the basic form read in this pattern, not reading.
Do not use reads after like; use reading or to read.
Like can take an -ing activity. Like to read would also be grammatical, but it is not one of these options.

findings: Flower-drawing item repeated enjoy and failed to teach an individual distinction.
audit.microSkill: Like with an -ing complement
audit.pedagogicalValue: Teaches one valid like pattern without falsely excluding like to read.
audit.levelReason: A simple leisure preference suits A1.
audit.similarityNote: Explicitly recognizes a verb that permits more than one complement form.

items.setupText: Complete this greeting with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: Hello, Eva. It's nice ___ you.
items.explanation: Nice to meet you is a common greeting when people first meet.

rationales.to meet: Nice to meet you is a common greeting when people first meet.
rationales.meet: In this greeting, use nice to meet, not nice meet.
rationales.to meeting: After to in this phrase, use meet without -ing.
rationales.met: Met is a past form; the greeting needs to meet.

findings: Door reminder rejected grammatical remembering without supplying a meaning criterion.
audit.microSkill: Nice to meet as a greeting
audit.pedagogicalValue: Introduces an adjective followed by a familiar infinitive phrase.
audit.levelReason: A routine first-meeting formula is accessible at A1.
audit.similarityNote: Social greeting replaces advanced remember-form ambiguity.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: Have you finished ___ your lunch?
items.explanation: Finish eating means completing the activity of eating.

rationales.eat: Finish needs the -ing form of the activity.
rationales.eating: Finish eating means completing the activity of eating.
rationales.to eat: Use finish eating, not finish to eat.
rationales.to eating: Do not put to before the -ing form after finish.

findings: Homework item supplied repeated generic feedback for all finish distractors.
audit.microSkill: Finish followed by an activity
audit.pedagogicalValue: Uses -ing to identify an activity that has ended.
audit.levelReason: A mealtime question provides familiar A1 language.
audit.similarityNote: Completing an activity differs from enjoying or starting one.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: Are you ready ___ home?
items.explanation: Ready to + verb says you are prepared for the action.

rationales.going: Ready is followed by to go in this sentence, not going alone.
rationales.go: Put to before go after ready.
rationales.to go: Ready to + verb says you are prepared for the action.
rationales.to went: Use go, not the past form went, after to.

findings: Clean-shirt item repeated need-to selection without useful feedback.
audit.microSkill: Ready to followed by an action
audit.pedagogicalValue: Connects being prepared with a next action.
audit.levelReason: A short question about going home suits A1.
audit.similarityNote: An adjective of readiness differs from a main verb selecting its complement.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: On Saturday mornings, I go ___ at the town market.
items.explanation: Go shopping is a common phrase for the activity of visiting shops to buy things.

rationales.shops: Shops cannot follow go to name this activity; use shopping.
rationales.to shopping: Do not add to before shopping in the activity phrase go shopping.
rationales.shopped: A past form does not follow go to name this activity.
rationales.shopping: Go shopping is a common phrase for the activity of visiting shops to buy things.

findings: Baby-playing item repeated enjoy with a childish setting and generic feedback.
audit.microSkill: Go shopping as an activity phrase
audit.pedagogicalValue: Introduces go followed by an -ing activity.
audit.levelReason: Routine shopping is familiar adult A1 content.
audit.similarityNote: An activity after go differs from an activity after enjoy.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: I want my brother ___ me tonight.
items.explanation: Use want + person + to + verb when you want another person to act.

rationales.to call: Use want + person + to + verb when you want another person to act.
rationales.called: Called me cannot follow I want my brother in this pattern; use my brother to call me.
rationales.calls: Calls is a finite verb; this want pattern needs to call.
rationales.to called: Use call, not called, after to.

findings: Lunch-bag forgetting item rejected bringing without establishing the intended meaning.
audit.microSkill: Want someone to do something
audit.pedagogicalValue: Identifies who should perform the wanted action.
audit.levelReason: A family phone call supports an A1 introduction to this common pattern.
audit.similarityNote: Different people want and perform the action.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: Nadia is good at ___ maps.
items.explanation: Use an -ing activity after good at: good at reading maps.

rationales.to read: After the preposition at, use reading rather than to read.
rationales.reading: Use an -ing activity after good at: good at reading maps.
rationales.reads: Reads cannot follow at to name an activity.
rationales.to reading: The needed preposition at is already present; do not add to.

findings: Story-reading item duplicated finish plus -ing without a new distinction.
audit.microSkill: Good at followed by -ing
audit.pedagogicalValue: Introduces an activity after a preposition in a familiar skill phrase.
audit.levelReason: Map reading and good at are accessible A1 expressions.
audit.similarityNote: At determines the following form, unlike the main-verb complement items.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: I'm thirsty. Is there something ___?
items.explanation: Something to drink means something available for a person to drink.

rationales.drinks: Drinks cannot directly follow something in this phrase.
rationales.to drinking: Use the basic verb drink after to here.
rationales.to drink: Something to drink means something available for a person to drink.
rationales.drank: The past form drank does not describe what something is available for.

findings: Window-seat wish repeated want-to grammar and generic messages.
audit.microSkill: Something followed by a to-infinitive
audit.pedagogicalValue: Names an available object through its possible use.
audit.levelReason: Thirst and a request for a drink are familiar A1 situations.
audit.similarityNote: The infinitive describes something rather than complementing a verb.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: Thank you for ___ me with these bags.
items.explanation: Thank you for + -ing expresses thanks for an action.

rationales.help: After for, use helping to name the action.
rationales.to help: For is followed by helping here, not a to-infinitive.
rationales.helped: Helped is a past form, but for needs the activity form helping.
rationales.helping: Thank you for + -ing expresses thanks for an action.

findings: Tea-drinking sentence recycled enjoy and its non-diagnostic feedback.
audit.microSkill: Thank you for plus -ing
audit.pedagogicalValue: Combines an action with a useful expression of thanks.
audit.levelReason: A short exchange about carrying bags fits A1.
audit.similarityNote: For introduces the action being thanked for.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: It's time ___ the shop.
items.explanation: It's time to + verb says the moment for that action has arrived.

rationales.to close: It's time to + verb says the moment for that action has arrived.
rationales.closing: Use time to close for this meaning, not time closing.
rationales.close: The action needs to after time in this phrase.
rationales.to closed: Use close rather than the past form closed after to.

findings: Bus-catching necessity was another need-to item with identical feedback logic.
audit.microSkill: Time to followed by a verb
audit.pedagogicalValue: Introduces an infinitive after a common time expression.
audit.levelReason: Closing a shop is concrete A1 work vocabulary.
audit.similarityNote: The infinitive follows time rather than a verb of wanting.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: Please stop ___ on the stairs.
items.explanation: Stop running asks someone to end the activity of running.

rationales.run: Stop needs running when the instruction is to end this activity.
rationales.running: Stop running asks someone to end the activity of running.
rationales.to running: Stop does not take to plus an -ing form here.
rationales.ran: A past form cannot follow stop in this instruction.

findings: Teacher-speaking context did not exclude the grammatical alternative stopped to talk.
audit.microSkill: Stop followed by the activity to end
audit.pedagogicalValue: Names the action a simple instruction asks someone to stop.
audit.levelReason: A short safety instruction is accessible at A1.
audit.similarityNote: Ends an activity; the later purpose contrast is reserved for higher levels.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: My partner wants ___ early for dinner.
items.explanation: Want takes to + basic verb, including be before an adjective.

rationales.is: Is cannot directly follow wants; use wants to be.
rationales.to being: After this to, use the basic form be.
rationales.to be: Want takes to + basic verb, including be before an adjective.
rationales.to is: The basic form is be, not is, after to.

findings: Friend-meeting hope was a repeated frame with generic form feedback.
audit.microSkill: The infinitive to be before an adjective
audit.pedagogicalValue: Shows how be changes when it follows to.
audit.levelReason: An arrival preference uses familiar A1 family and time language.
audit.similarityNote: Focuses on be rather than an ordinary action verb.

items.setupText: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
items.taskText: Describe the start of your work on a letter.
options: I started to wrote the letter.
items.explanation: Start can take writing. Started to write would also be correct, but it is not offered here.

Writes cannot follow started to name the next action.
After to, the basic form would be write, not wrote.
Start needs writing or to write, not write alone.
Start can take writing. Started to write would also be correct, but it is not offered here.

findings: Kitchen-cooking item was another enjoy-plus-ing repetition.
audit.microSkill: Start with an -ing complement
audit.pedagogicalValue: Teaches one valid start pattern while acknowledging the other.
audit.levelReason: A brief writing action suits A1 foundation practice.
audit.similarityNote: Starting an activity contrasts with finishing lunch and stopping movement.

items.setupText: Choose the sentence saying that taking a walk gives you pleasure.
items.taskText: What can you say about your free time?
options: I need to walk after dinner.
I forgot to walk after dinner.
I agreed to walk after dinner.
items.explanation: Enjoy walking says the activity is pleasant for you.

Enjoy walking says the activity is pleasant for you.
Need to describes something necessary, not something you enjoy.
Forgot to says an intended walk did not happen because you forgot it.
Agreed to accepts a plan for a walk; it does not say that you enjoy walking.

findings: Pre-movie leaving sentence repeated need to and boilerplate explanations.
audit.microSkill: Meaning of an enjoyment complement
audit.pedagogicalValue: Connects a verb pattern with pleasure rather than necessity or memory.
audit.levelReason: A common free-time routine supports simple A1 meaning selection.
audit.similarityNote: Meaning selection complements the earlier enjoy form question without reusing its frame.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: Please wash your hands before ___ the food.
items.explanation: After before, an -ing form can name the action: before touching the food.

rationales.to touch: Before does not take a to-infinitive for this action.
rationales.touching: After before, an -ing form can name the action: before touching the food.
rationales.touches: A clause with touches would need its own subject; this phrase uses touching.
rationales.to touching: Do not insert to between before and touching.

findings: Short-story item repeated A1 enjoy grammar and boilerplate feedback.
audit.microSkill: Before followed by an -ing phrase
audit.pedagogicalValue: Links a first action to a later one without repeating the subject.
audit.levelReason: A practical food instruction supports A2 sequencing.
audit.similarityNote: Time preposition differs from enjoyment and purpose patterns.

items.setupText: Choose the meaning of the completed action.
items.taskText: 'We finished painting the kitchen yesterday.'
options: We planned to begin painting the kitchen yesterday.
We paused another job so that we could paint the kitchen.
The kitchen painting was completed yesterday.
We decided against painting the kitchen yesterday.
items.answer: The kitchen painting was completed yesterday.
items.explanation: Finished painting says the activity reached its end.

rationales.The kitchen painting was completed yeste: Finished painting says the activity reached its end.
rationales.We planned to begin painting the kitchen: Finish does not describe planning to start an activity.
rationales.We paused another job so that we could p: A pause for another purpose would use stopped to paint, not finished painting.
rationales.We decided against painting the kitchen: Deciding not to paint does not match an activity that was finished.

findings: Worksheet item repeated finish form selection without specific feedback.
audit.microSkill: Finished doing as completion
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes completed work from planning, a purpose, and rejection.
audit.levelReason: A short account of home maintenance fits A2.
audit.similarityNote: Interprets completion instead of repeating A1 finish-form selection.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: The room was too expensive, so we decided ___ it.
items.explanation: Decide not to + verb expresses a decision against an action.

rationales.not booking: Decide needs an infinitive or a clause here; use decided not to book.
rationales.not book: The infinitive after decided requires to.
rationales.not to booked: Use the basic verb book after to.
rationales.not to book: Decide not to + verb expresses a decision against an action.

findings: Office-call item used generic feedback and only an affirmative decide pattern.
audit.microSkill: Negative infinitive after decide
audit.pedagogicalValue: Expresses a choice not to perform an action.
audit.levelReason: An expensive room gives a clear A2 reason for a negative decision.
audit.similarityNote: Negative intention contrasts with other affirmative complements.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: To keep the entrance clear, avoid ___ beside the gate.
items.explanation: Avoid + -ing identifies the activity you should not do.

rationales.to park: Avoid takes parking, not to park.
rationales.parking: Avoid + -ing identifies the activity you should not do.
rationales.to parking: Avoid does not take the added preposition to in this pattern.

findings: Exam-room talking used undifferentiated feedback for avoid distractors.
audit.microSkill: Avoid plus an -ing complement
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes the purpose infinitive from the activity following avoid.
audit.levelReason: A familiar parking instruction contains manageable A2 phrase contrasts.
audit.similarityNote: Two different verb forms serve different roles in one instruction.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: The mechanic promised ___ me when the car was ready.
items.explanation: Promise to + verb states an action the speaker commits to doing.

rationales.texting: A promised action uses promise to text here, not promise texting.
rationales.to text: Promise to + verb states an action the speaker commits to doing.
rationales.texted: The past form texted cannot directly complete promised in this pattern.
rationales.to texting: After this to, use text without -ing.

findings: Teacher-results sentence had boilerplate feedback and another classroom setting.
audit.microSkill: Promise followed by an infinitive
audit.pedagogicalValue: Connects a commitment to its future action.
audit.levelReason: A car-repair notification is practical A2 service language.
audit.similarityNote: Commitment differs from an expectation or a wish.

items.setupText: Choose who accepts the extra shift in this sentence.
items.taskText: 'After talking to Jo, Leila agreed to cover the evening shift.'
options: Leila asks Jo to accept the extra work.
items.explanation: With agreed to cover, the subject Leila is also the person who will cover the shift.

With agreed to cover, the subject Leila is also the person who will cover the shift.
Jo is part of the earlier conversation, not the subject of agreed to cover.
Agreed to cover describes Leila's agreement, not a request to Jo.

findings: Chair-moving item wrongly rejected agreed to moving, which can be grammatical.
audit.microSkill: Performer of an action after agree to
audit.pedagogicalValue: Tracks the shared subject of agree and its infinitive.
audit.levelReason: Two named adults in a shift exchange support A2 reference tracking.
audit.similarityNote: Meaning task avoids falsely making agree to plus -ing ungrammatical.

items.setupText: Choose the meaning of kept checking.
items.taskText: 'While waiting for the delivery, I kept checking my phone.'
options: I saved my phone so that I could check it later.
I checked my phone repeatedly during the wait.
I remembered one earlier occasion when I checked my phone.
I tried to avoid checking my phone during the wait.
items.answer: I checked my phone repeatedly during the wait.
items.explanation: Keep + -ing can describe an action that continues or happens repeatedly.

rationales.I saved my phone so that I could check i: Kept followed by checking means repeated action, not storing the phone.
rationales.I remembered one earlier occasion when I: That would describe a memory, not repeated checking during the wait.
rationales.I checked my phone repeatedly during the: Keep + -ing can describe an action that continues or happens repeatedly.
rationales.I tried to avoid checking my phone durin: Avoid checking is the opposite of the repeated action described.

findings: Video-notes item supplied generic keep-pattern feedback without explaining continuation.
audit.microSkill: Keep doing as repeated action
audit.pedagogicalValue: Interprets keep beyond its ordinary meaning of possession.
audit.levelReason: Waiting for a delivery gives an accessible A2 repeated-action context.
audit.similarityNote: Repetition differs from completion and avoidance.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: This diagram shows you how ___ the shelf.

rationales.fitting: After how in this instruction phrase, use to fit rather than fitting.
rationales.fit: The phrase is how to fit, not how fit.
rationales.to fitted: Use the basic form fit after to.
rationales.to fit: How to + verb can name a method or explain an action.

findings: New-job hope repeated beginner infinitive selection with boilerplate.
audit.microSkill: How followed by a to-infinitive
audit.pedagogicalValue: Recognizes a compact phrase describing a method.
audit.levelReason: A household diagram gives concrete A2 support.
audit.similarityNote: The infinitive follows a question word, not a lexical verb.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: I left the house without ___ my umbrella.

rationales.to take: Without takes an -ing phrase rather than to take.
rationales.taking: Without taking says the departure happened but taking the umbrella did not.
rationales.took: Took is a past verb; without needs taking in this phrase.
rationales.to taking: Do not add to after without.

findings: Repeated-question avoidance recycled avoid grammar and generic feedback.
audit.microSkill: Without plus -ing
audit.pedagogicalValue: Describes an action missing from another event.
audit.levelReason: A forgotten everyday object gives clear A2 context.
audit.similarityNote: Absence of an accompanying action differs from a negative decision.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: When my bicycle broke, a neighbor offered ___ me home.

rationales.to drive: Offer to + verb proposes an action the person offering will perform.
rationales.driving: After offered, the proposed action uses to drive here.
rationales.drive: The infinitive after offered needs to.
rationales.to drove: Use drive rather than the past form drove after to.

findings: New-student help sentence supplied only generic offer-pattern feedback.
audit.microSkill: Offer followed by an infinitive
audit.pedagogicalValue: Connects an offer of help to the helper's action.
audit.levelReason: A neighbor helping with transport is a concrete A2 exchange.
audit.similarityNote: Volunteered help differs from a promise or accepted duty.

items.setupText: Choose the activity form that says what occupied the whole hour.
items.taskText: We spent an hour ___ the new desk.

rationales.to assemble: After spend time, use assembling to name the activity.
rationales.assemble: The basic verb cannot directly follow an hour in this spend-time pattern.
rationales.assembling: Spend + time + -ing says how the time was used.
rationales.to assembling: Do not insert to before the -ing activity after spent an hour.

findings: Sugar-in-tea item tested quit with repeated boilerplate explanations.

audit.pedagogicalValue: Expresses the activity occupying a measured period.
audit.levelReason: Furniture assembly and one hour are accessible A2 details.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.

audit.pedagogicalValue: Relates size to an action that cannot be achieved.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: Before the interview, I practiced ___ myself in English.

items.taskText: Since moving inland, I miss ___ beside the sea.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: My aunt taught me ___ a bicycle tire.
items.explanation: Teach + person + to + verb identifies the learner and the skill taught.

rationales.changing: In taught me + action, use to change rather than changing.
rationales.changed: Changed is a past form, not the infinitive needed after taught me.
rationales.to changing: This to requires the basic form change.
rationales.to change: Teach + person + to + verb identifies the learner and the skill taught.

findings: Email-learning sentence used boilerplate and another classroom-centered frame.
audit.microSkill: Teach someone to do something
audit.pedagogicalValue: Locates the learner before the infinitive naming the skill.
audit.levelReason: A practical family-taught skill suits A2.
audit.similarityNote: Skill teaching introduces a different relation between two participants.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: The receptionist suggested ___ the earlier bus.
items.explanation: Suggest takes an -ing activity here: suggested taking the earlier bus.

rationales.taking: Suggest takes an -ing activity here: suggested taking the earlier bus.
rationales.to take: Do not directly follow suggested with to take in this pattern.
rationales.take: A clause with take would need a subject, as in suggested that we take.
rationales.to taking: Suggest does not require an extra to before taking.

findings: Water suggestion had undifferentiated feedback and no contrast with a valid that-clause.
audit.microSkill: Suggest plus an activity
audit.pedagogicalValue: Recognizes the -ing pattern while acknowledging a separate clause alternative.
audit.levelReason: A transport suggestion is useful A2 service language.
audit.similarityNote: Advice is expressed as an activity rather than a command to a person.

items.setupText: Choose the sentence meaning that the customer would not provide an address.
items.taskText: The clerk asked for the address twice.
options: The customer refused to give an address.
The customer forgot to give an address.
The customer offered to give an address.
The customer hoped to give an address.
items.answer: The customer refused to give an address.
items.explanation: Refused to + verb expresses unwillingness to perform the requested action.

Forgot to describes an omission caused by memory, not an unwilling response to the requests.
Offered to volunteers the action rather than refusing it.
Refused to + verb expresses unwillingness to perform the requested action.
Hoped to expresses a desired action, not refusal.

findings: Driver refusing to leave without a ticket was awkwardly motivated and had generic feedback.
audit.microSkill: Refuse to as unwillingness
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes refusal from forgetting, offering, and hoping.
audit.levelReason: A short customer-service incident supports A2 meaning selection.
audit.similarityNote: Unwillingness differs from a negative decision based on cost.

items.setupText: Complete the polite request with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: Would you mind ___ the window? It's cold in here.
items.explanation: Would you mind + -ing is a polite way to ask someone to act.

rationales.to close: Mind takes closing, not to close, in this request.
rationales.closing: Would you mind + -ing is a polite way to ask someone to act.
rationales.close: Use the -ing form after mind, not the basic verb alone.
rationales.to closing: Do not put to before closing after mind.

findings: Children kept dancing item duplicated keep practice and had unclear sequencing.
audit.microSkill: Would you mind plus -ing
audit.pedagogicalValue: Builds a common polite request through an activity complement.
audit.levelReason: The familiar request can be learned as an A2 phrase.
audit.similarityNote: Polite mind-plus-ing differs from modal requests in the modals topic.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: The host asked us ___ our shoes inside.
items.explanation: Ask + person + not to + verb reports a request against an action.

rationales.don't wear: After asked us, use an infinitive phrase, not the direct instruction don't wear.
rationales.not wearing: This reported request needs not to wear after us.
rationales.not to wore: Use wear rather than wore after to.
rationales.not to wear: Ask + person + not to + verb reports a request against an action.

findings: Last-page reminder repeated basic positive to-form choices with generic feedback.
audit.microSkill: Ask someone not to do something
audit.pedagogicalValue: Reports a negative request while identifying its recipient.
audit.levelReason: A house rule is a clear A2 social context.
audit.similarityNote: Negative request to someone differs from one's own negative decision.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: After a long discussion, the neighbors agreed on ___ the shared fence.
items.explanation: Agree on + -ing names the action people have jointly selected.

rationales.to repair: The preposition on needs repairing, not a to-infinitive.
rationales.repairing: Agree on + -ing names the action people have jointly selected.
rationales.repair: The noun would need wording such as the repair of the fence; this action phrase needs repairing the fence.
rationales.repaired: Repaired is not the activity form required after on.

findings: Front-office deadline item repeated elementary agree selection and generic feedback.
audit.microSkill: Agree on followed by an activity
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes a prepositional complement from agree to do.
audit.levelReason: A negotiated shared action suits B1 verb-pattern precision.
audit.similarityNote: A fixed preposition determines the form rather than a bare lexical verb.

items.setupText: Both forms in one option can complete the sentence correctly. Choose that pair.
items.taskText: Carlos admitted ___ the wrong file.
items.explanation: Both admit doing and admit to doing are grammatical; to is a preposition in the second pattern.

rationales.opening / to opening: Both admit doing and admit to doing are grammatical; to is a preposition in the second pattern.
rationales.opening / to open: Opening works, but admitted to open does not express this admission; use to opening.
rationales.open / to opening: To opening works, but the basic form open cannot directly follow admitted here.
rationales.to open / open: Neither the to-infinitive nor the basic form fits this admission pattern.

findings: Original incorrectly marked admitted to opening wrong, creating two correct options.
audit.microSkill: Two accepted complement patterns after admit
audit.pedagogicalValue: Recognizes a genuine grammatical alternative instead of memorizing a false restriction.
audit.levelReason: Comparing two valid patterns is a useful B1 extension of verb complementation.
audit.similarityNote: Only B1 task asking for a pair of equally valid forms.

items.setupText: The passport is still on the table. Complete the reminder about what Leo must do before leaving.
items.taskText: Leo, remember ___ your passport.
items.explanation: Remember to pack means keep the task in mind and do it before leaving.

rationales.packing: Remember packing recalls a previous action; this reminder concerns an action still to do.
rationales.pack: Remember needs to pack for a future duty, not pack alone.
rationales.to packing: Use the basic form pack after to in this reminder.
rationales.to pack: Remember to pack means keep the task in mind and do it before leaving.

findings: Manager-refusal item repeated a basic infinitive frame without meaningful B1 distinction.
audit.microSkill: Remember to do a pending action
audit.pedagogicalValue: Uses the event's timing to choose between remembering patterns.
audit.levelReason: A pending travel task provides B1 support for a meaning-changing complement.
audit.similarityNote: Prospective memory contrasts with recollection in item 1484.

items.setupText: The speaker describes a clear memory from yesterday. Complete the sentence with that meaning.
items.taskText: I remember ___ the parcel to the receptionist; she thanked me for it.
items.explanation: Remember + -ing recalls an experience; the thanks is a detail of that remembered event.

rationales.to hand: Remember to hand concerns remembering a task to perform, not recollecting the scene described.
rationales.hand: The basic form hand cannot directly complete remember here.
rationales.handing: Remember + -ing recalls an experience; the thanks is a detail of that remembered event.
rationales.to handing: This memory pattern takes handing without to.

findings: Reading-class practice item repeated elementary -ing selection and boilerplate.
audit.microSkill: Remember doing a past event
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes recalling an event from remembering a duty.
audit.levelReason: A remembered interaction gives concrete evidence for a B1 meaning contrast.
audit.similarityNote: Recollected performance differs from the pending passport task.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: Despite the noise, the interpreter managed ___ the final question.
items.explanation: Manage to + verb reports success despite a difficulty.

rationales.hearing: Manage meaning succeed takes to hear, not hearing directly.
rationales.to hear: Manage to + verb reports success despite a difficulty.
rationales.hear: Put to before the action after managed.
rationales.to heard: Use the basic form hear, not heard, after to.

findings: Missing-receipt sentence gave no explanation of manage as successful achievement.
audit.microSkill: Manage to expressing achieved action
audit.pedagogicalValue: Connects the infinitive pattern with success under difficult conditions.
audit.levelReason: A contrast clause and a completed achievement suit B1.
audit.similarityNote: Pattern formation with a perception verb differs from the modals topic's outcome comparison.

items.setupText: The driver was travelling, saw a cafe, and took a break there. Complete the sentence to explain the purpose of the stop.
items.taskText: She stopped ___ a coffee.
items.explanation: Stop to + verb means pause another activity in order to do this action.

rationales.to buy: Stop to + verb means pause another activity in order to do this action.
rationales.buying: Stopped buying would mean she ended the activity of buying coffee.
rationales.buy: The purpose of the stop needs to buy, not buy alone.
rationales.to buying: A purpose infinitive uses the basic form buy after to.

findings: Admissions-office deadline item merely swapped nouns in an agree-to frame.
audit.microSkill: Stop to do as purpose of a pause
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes interrupting travel to buy from ending repeated buying.
audit.levelReason: A short travel sequence makes the B1 meaning contrast explicit.
audit.similarityNote: Purpose of stopping differs from the A1 instruction to stop an activity.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence to describe an experience that remains vivid in the speaker's memory.
items.taskText: I'll never forget ___ the northern lights for the first time.
items.explanation: Never forget + -ing describes a past experience that remains memorable.

rationales.to see: Forget to see would concern failing to carry out a task, not remembering an experience.
rationales.see: Forget cannot take see alone to name this memory.
rationales.seeing: Never forget + -ing describes a past experience that remains memorable.
rationales.to seeing: Use seeing without to after forget in this memory pattern.

findings: Sofia admission repeated a two-answer error involving admitted to opening.
audit.microSkill: Forget doing as loss of a memory
audit.pedagogicalValue: Recognizes the experience recalled in never forget doing.
audit.levelReason: A memorable travel experience supports B1 temporal interpretation.
audit.similarityNote: A lasting memory differs from remembering to complete an obligation.

items.setupText: The screen keeps freezing. Complete the technician's suggestion for testing a possible solution.
items.taskText: Try ___ the browser and see whether that helps.
items.explanation: Try + -ing suggests doing something as an experiment to see whether it solves a problem.

rationales.restart: Try needs restarting or to restart as a complement, not restart alone here.
rationales.to restarting: Do not combine to with restarting in this pattern.
rationales.restarted: Restarted is a past form; it cannot name the proposed experiment after try.
rationales.restarting: Try + -ing suggests doing something as an experiment to see whether it solves a problem.

findings: Service-manager refusal was a near-duplicate without new learning value.
audit.microSkill: Try doing as a possible solution
audit.pedagogicalValue: Relates the -ing form to testing a method.
audit.levelReason: A technical-help suggestion is familiar B1 functional language.
audit.similarityNote: The experiment concerns a readily performed action rather than a difficult attempt.

items.setupText: The speaker intended to reply, but the reply was never sent. Choose the completion preserving that meaning.
items.taskText: I meant ___ your message yesterday.
items.explanation: Mean to + verb expresses an intention; the context shows it was not carried out.

rationales.answering: Meant answering would mean involved answering, not intended to answer.
rationales.to answer: Mean to + verb expresses an intention; the context shows it was not carried out.
rationales.answer: The intended action needs to before answer after meant.
rationales.to answering: This to is followed by the basic verb answer, not answering.

findings: Saturday-class practice item repeated a basic asking pattern with only the class label changed.
audit.microSkill: Mean to do as intention
audit.pedagogicalValue: Separates intention from the involving meaning of mean doing.
audit.levelReason: An apology for a missed reply supports B1 complement interpretation.
audit.similarityNote: Intention is distinct from remembering, agreeing, or succeeding.

items.setupText: The speaker sold the bicycle last year and now wishes they had kept it. Choose the completion that describes this regret.
items.taskText: I regret ___ my old bicycle.
items.explanation: Regret + -ing expresses unhappiness about an earlier action, here the completed sale.

rationales.selling: Regret + -ing expresses unhappiness about an earlier action, here the completed sale.
rationales.to sell: Regret to is used especially when announcing unwelcome information; it does not describe this completed sale.
rationales.sell: Regret does not directly take the basic form sell in this meaning.
rationales.to selling: The past action after regret uses selling without to.

findings: Mateo receipt sentence repeated manage-to selection with no fresh distinction.
audit.microSkill: Regret doing a past action
audit.pedagogicalValue: Links regret to an action already performed.
audit.levelReason: A concrete past choice supports B1 retrospective meaning.
audit.similarityNote: Regretted performance differs from an unrealized intention.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: We're looking forward to ___ the new neighbors at dinner.
items.explanation: Look forward to takes an -ing activity because to is a preposition here.

rationales.meet: To in look forward to is a preposition, so the action takes -ing.
rationales.to meet: The existing to belongs to look forward to; do not add another to-infinitive.
rationales.meeting: Look forward to takes an -ing activity because to is a preposition here.
rationales.met: Met is a past form, not the activity form required after this to.

findings: Finance-office lesson-plan deadline recycled agree-to grammar and an unlikely ownership context.
audit.microSkill: Prepositional to in look forward to
audit.pedagogicalValue: Shows that to does not invariably introduce a basic verb.
audit.levelReason: An anticipated social event grounds a B1 preposition-versus-infinitive distinction.
audit.similarityNote: Positive anticipation contrasts with objection after another prepositional to.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: The residents objected to ___ the only local bus route.
items.explanation: Object to + -ing names the action or situation a person opposes.

rationales.lose: Object to takes an -ing action because to is a preposition.
rationales.lost: Lost cannot follow to here to name the action opposed.
rationales.to lose: Do not add a second to before the action after objected to.
rationales.losing: Object to + -ing names the action or situation a person opposes.

findings: Jonas admission item again rejected the grammatical admitted to opening.
audit.microSkill: Object to followed by an -ing clause
audit.pedagogicalValue: Links an objection to its content without confusing prepositional to with an infinitive.
audit.levelReason: A community transport issue gives a meaningful B1 context.
audit.similarityNote: Opposition differs from anticipating a welcome event.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: The owner allows guests ___ bicycles in the courtyard.
items.explanation: Allow + person + to + verb identifies who has permission and what they may do.

rationales.to leave: Allow + person + to + verb identifies who has permission and what they may do.
rationales.to leaving: After allow guests to, use the basic form leave, not leaving.
rationales.leave: Unlike let, allow needs to before the following action verb.
rationales.to left: The infinitive uses leave, not left.

findings: Department-manager refusal sentence was another noun-swapped duplicate.
audit.microSkill: Allow someone to do versus let someone do
audit.pedagogicalValue: Prepares the contrast between two permission verbs with different complements.
audit.levelReason: A shared-building rule supports a B1 object-plus-infinitive pattern.
audit.similarityNote: Permission is expressed with allow, which requires to before the action.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: The unexpected alarm made everyone ___ the room.
items.explanation: Active make takes a person followed by the basic verb: made everyone leave.

rationales.to leave: In the active pattern make + person + verb, leave has no to.
rationales.leave: Active make takes a person followed by the basic verb: made everyone leave.
rationales.leaving: Leaving does not complete this active causative pattern.
rationales.left: Use the basic form leave, not the past form left, after made everyone.

findings: Summer-class asking item repeated practice with identical feedback logic.
audit.microSkill: Make someone do in an active causative
audit.pedagogicalValue: Uses a basic verb without to when something causes another person's action.
audit.levelReason: A clear cause and reaction supports B1 causative grammar.
audit.similarityNote: Causing an action differs from allowing it.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: My supervisor let me ___ the afternoon meeting online.
items.explanation: Use let + person + basic verb to express permission.

rationales.to join: Let takes the basic verb without to: let me join.
rationales.joining: The person after let is followed by join, not joining.
rationales.join: Use let + person + basic verb to express permission.
rationales.joined: Joined is a past form; let me requires the basic verb join.

findings: Sara receipt sentence was a name-only manage-to repetition.
audit.microSkill: Let someone do without to
audit.pedagogicalValue: Contrasts let with allow while preserving the permission meaning.
audit.levelReason: Joining a work meeting is a familiar B1 situation.
audit.similarityNote: Bare infinitive after let contrasts with the allow pattern in item 1493.

items.setupText: Choose the reported warning that preserves the electrician's instruction.
items.taskText: The electrician said to us, 'Do not touch those wires.'
options: The electrician warned us not to touch the wires.
The electrician warned us to touch the wires.
The electrician warned not to touch us with the wires.
The electrician warned us touching the wires.
items.answer: The electrician warned us not to touch the wires.
items.explanation: Warn + person + not to + verb preserves both the recipient and the negative instruction.

rationales.The electrician warned us to touch the w: This reverses the warning by instructing you to touch them.
rationales.The electrician warned not to touch us w: This changes who is touched and does not preserve the original instruction.
rationales.The electrician warned us touching the w: The reported instruction needs not to touch after us.
rationales.The electrician warned us not to touch t: Warn + person + not to + verb preserves both the recipient and the negative instruction.

findings: Reception-office deadline sentence recycled agree-to grammar with a substituted object.
audit.microSkill: Reporting a negative warning with an infinitive
audit.pedagogicalValue: Preserves the participants and negation when reporting direct speech.
audit.levelReason: Transforming a short safety instruction adds B1 control beyond form selection.
audit.similarityNote: A meaning-preserving reported warning differs from a direct gap-fill request.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: A fallen tree prevented the bus from ___ the village.
items.explanation: Prevent + object + from + -ing describes an action that something blocks.

rationales.to reach: After from, use reaching rather than to reach.
rationales.reaching: Prevent + object + from + -ing describes an action that something blocks.
rationales.reach: The preposition from needs the -ing action form here.
rationales.reached: Reached cannot follow from as the action being prevented.

findings: Emma admission repeated the same two-correct-answer defect.
audit.microSkill: Prevent someone or something from doing
audit.pedagogicalValue: Separates the obstacle, affected participant, and blocked action.
audit.levelReason: A road obstruction provides a concrete B1 multi-part verb pattern.
audit.similarityNote: Prevention differs from refusal, permission, and causation.

items.setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: With rent increasing, we're considering ___ to a smaller office.
items.explanation: Consider + -ing means think about an action as a possible choice.

rationales.moving: Consider + -ing means think about an action as a possible choice.
rationales.to move: Consider does not directly take to move in this planning meaning.
rationales.move: The basic form move cannot complete considering here.
rationales.to moving: No to is needed before moving after considering.

findings: Payroll-manager refusal sentence repeated the same elementary pattern and feedback.
audit.microSkill: Consider doing as an option under discussion
audit.pedagogicalValue: Names an action being evaluated without saying it is decided.
audit.levelReason: A practical office decision suits B1 planning language.
audit.similarityNote: An undecided option contrasts with agreed, intended, and refused actions.

items.setupText: Complete the comparison with the correct grammar.
items.taskText: For short journeys, I prefer cycling to ___ a car.
items.explanation: Prefer + -ing + to + -ing compares two activities using parallel forms.

rationales.drive: In prefer cycling to, to is a preposition; use driving as the compared activity.
rationales.to drive: Do not add a second to when comparing activities with prefer cycling to.
rationales.driving: Prefer + -ing + to + -ing compares two activities using parallel forms.
rationales.drove: The past form drove cannot name the second activity after this to.

findings: Final-class asking sentence repeated practice with only the class description changed.
audit.microSkill: Prefer doing to doing
audit.pedagogicalValue: Keeps comparable activities in matching forms after a prepositional to.
audit.levelReason: A transport preference supports B1 parallel-complement grammar.
audit.similarityNote: A comparison of activities differs from look-forward-to or object-to complements.

items.setupText: Choose the pair that completes both phrases correctly.
items.taskText: The hilltop museum is worth ___ and easy ___.
items.explanation: Worth takes an -ing activity; easy takes a to-infinitive describing what can be done to the subject.

rationales.to visit / reaching: Worth takes visiting, while easy takes to reach in this sentence.
rationales.visiting / reaching: Visiting fits worth, but easy needs to reach rather than reaching.
rationales.to visit / to reach: To reach fits easy, but worth needs visiting.
rationales.visiting / to reach: Worth takes an -ing activity; easy takes a to-infinitive describing what can be done to the subject.

findings: Theo receipt sentence was the fourth name-only manage-to duplicate.
audit.microSkill: Different complements after worth and easy
audit.pedagogicalValue: Chooses a complement based on its actual leading expression, not one rule for all adjectives.
audit.levelReason: Two familiar travel descriptions support an integrative B1 pattern contrast.
audit.similarityNote: Paired adjective complements differ from pairs of valid admit forms.

items.setupText: The photographer stayed behind the screen so that visitors would not see her. Preserve who sees whom.
items.taskText: She avoided ___ by the visitors.
items.explanation: Avoid takes an -ing form; being seen makes her the person receiving the visitors' attention.

rationales.seeing: Seeing makes her the observer, whereas the visitors would see her.
rationales.being seen: Avoid takes an -ing form; being seen makes her the person receiving the visitors' attention.
rationales.to be seen: The passive meaning fits, but avoid needs being seen rather than to be seen.
rationales.having seen: Having seen makes her the person who had observed something, reversing the roles.

findings: Mistake-avoidance item tested basic -ing selection at B2 with generic feedback.
audit.microSkill: Passive gerund after avoid
audit.pedagogicalValue: Combines complement selection with the direction of the action.
audit.levelReason: Tracking voice as well as the governing verb supports B2.
audit.similarityNote: Avoidance concerns being observed rather than performing an action.

items.setupText: Rewrite the judgment with the camera as subject, preserving the present assessment.
items.taskText: 'Reviewers consider this camera reliable.' This camera is considered ___.
items.explanation: Is considered to be reports an assessment of the subject; this differs from consider doing an action.

rationales.being reliable: Passive considered uses to be here, not an -ing clause naming an option under consideration.
rationales.to have been reliable: The perfect phrase places the reliability earlier instead of preserving the present assessment.
rationales.to be reliable: Is considered to be reports an assessment of the subject; this differs from consider doing an action.
rationales.reliably: Reliably describes how something acts; the judgment is that the camera itself is reliable.

findings: Deadline-consideration item reused a basic pattern and five-frame cycle.
audit.microSkill: Passive consider with a to-infinitive
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes consider as evaluate from consider as contemplate an action.
audit.levelReason: A passive rewrite with a changed complement structure suits B2.
audit.similarityNote: Judgment of a quality differs from B1 considering relocation.

items.setupText: Use the perfect infinitive to make completion before the inspection explicit.
items.taskText: The builder expects ___ the roof by the time the inspector arrives.
items.explanation: To have + past participle presents repair as complete before the inspection time.

rationales.to have repaired: To have + past participle presents repair as complete before the inspection time.
rationales.to having repaired: After infinitival to, use have rather than having.
rationales.having repaired: Expect does not directly take this -ing clause for the expected action.
rationales.to have repairing: Have needs repaired, not repairing, in the perfect infinitive.

findings: Reply expectation had an unnecessary budget-meeting tail and only elementary form choices.
audit.microSkill: Perfect infinitive after expect
audit.pedagogicalValue: Makes relative completion time explicit inside an expectation.
audit.levelReason: A deadline linked to another event supports B2 perfect-time control.
audit.similarityNote: The infinitive describes a completed state at a future reference point.

items.setupText: Choose the pair that completes both linked verb patterns correctly.
items.taskText: The panel postponed ___ whom ___ until all applications were in.
items.explanation: Postpone takes an -ing activity; decide can be followed by a question-word phrase with a to-infinitive.

rationales.deciding / interviewing: Deciding fits postponed, but the embedded choice uses whom to interview, not whom interviewing.
rationales.to decide / interviewing: Postpone needs deciding, and the embedded question needs whom to interview.
rationales.to decide / to interview: To interview fits after whom, but postpone takes deciding rather than to decide.
rationales.deciding / to interview: Postpone takes an -ing activity; decide can be followed by a question-word phrase with a to-infinitive.

findings: Training-manager postponement repeated simple -ing selection with generic feedback.
audit.microSkill: An infinitival question within a gerund complement
audit.pedagogicalValue: Selects each form according to its local governing expression.
audit.levelReason: Two nested complement patterns create an integrative B2 decision.
audit.similarityNote: The action postponed is deciding which later action to arrange.

items.setupText: Choose the rewrite that says the team made a decision against publication.
items.taskText: 'The team decided that it would not publish the survey yet.'
options: The team decided not to publish the survey yet.
The team did not decide to publish the survey yet.
The team decided publishing the survey not yet.
The team decided to publish the survey yet.
items.answer: The team decided not to publish the survey yet.
items.explanation: Not belongs to the infinitive, so the decision is specifically to withhold publication.

rationales.The team did not decide to publish the s: This says no positive publication decision was made; it need not mean a decision against publication was made.
rationales.The team decided not to publish the surv: Not belongs to the infinitive, so the decision is specifically to withhold publication.
rationales.The team decided publishing the survey n: This is not the required decide-plus-infinitive pattern, and not yet is misplaced.
rationales.The team decided to publish the survey y: This removes the decision against publication and leaves yet without the intended negative context.

findings: Survey-planning item had a repeated after-the-meeting tail and no B2 distinction.
audit.microSkill: Negation of a decision versus a decision not to act
audit.pedagogicalValue: Preserves which proposition is negative during a rewrite.
audit.levelReason: Negation placement changes what the sentence commits the writer to, a B2 precision task.
audit.similarityNote: Negation scope is compared rather than merely forming a negative infinitive.

items.setupText: Read the complete account. Choose the conclusion it supports.
items.taskText: 'I tried to open the jammed drawer for ten minutes, but eventually called a carpenter.'
options: The speaker opened it by experimenting with a new technique.
The speaker avoided attempting to open it until help arrived.
The speaker remembers opening it before it became jammed.
The speaker attempted to open it; the account does not report success.
items.answer: The speaker attempted to open it; the account does not report success.
items.explanation: Try to + verb expresses an effort toward an action; it does not itself assert achievement.

rationales.The speaker opened it by experimenting w: The account supplies neither a successful opening nor a newly tested method.
rationales.The speaker avoided attempting to open i: Tried to open explicitly states that an attempt was made.
rationales.The speaker attempted to open it; the ac: Try to + verb expresses an effort toward an action; it does not itself assert achievement.
rationales.The speaker remembers opening it before: This is an attempt at the jammed drawer, not recollection of an earlier opening.

findings: Lena mistake item was a name-only avoid duplicate.
audit.microSkill: Try to as an attempt without an entailment of success
audit.pedagogicalValue: Separates attempting an action from completing it.
audit.levelReason: Reading what a complement does and does not establish suits B2 inference.
audit.similarityNote: An effort toward a difficult result differs from trying a suggested method.

items.setupText: The technician gave the speaker a warning last week. Complete the speaker's memory of receiving that warning.
items.taskText: I remember ___ not to unplug the device during the update.
items.explanation: Remember being told recalls receiving someone else's instruction.

rationales.being told: Remember being told recalls receiving someone else's instruction.

items.setupText: Compare (1) 'The author acknowledged overstating the claim in last year's paper' and (2) 'The author acknowledged having overstated the claim in last year's paper.'

The first reports an admission, whereas the second gives independent proof that the claim was overstated.
items.answer: Both can describe the same earlier act; the perfect form marks its priority explicitly.

rationales.The first leaves the author's responsibi: The author is understood as the person responsible for overstating in both complements; perfect form does not change that role.

It does not go as far as recommending withdrawal.

rationales.It does not go as far as recommending wi: Stop short of + -ing identifies a step or claim that is not taken despite movement in that direction.

items.setupText: A journalist asks whether closure is impossible. The spokesperson's response is summarized below. Choose what can be concluded.

rationales.The spokesperson did not exclude closure: Declined to rule out withholds an exclusion; closing names the option that remains unexcluded.

items.setupText: The client received the revised estimate only after approving the work. Interpret the complaint.

She objects because she was informed before approving the work.

items.setupText: The team assigned entry checks to assistants in an attempt to reduce errors. Choose the rewrite making these roles explicit without asserting successful error reduction.

items.setupText: Compare the accounts as their narrators present them. Choose the distinction between the embedded actions.

findings: Corrigendum acknowledgment item repeated a perfect-gerund template with inflated context.
